passages.text: Now the first covenant had regulations for worship and also an earthly sanctuary.
passages.sermon: The first covenant was given by God to Israel.\r\nThis covenant had rules for worship.\r\nIt also had a sanctuary on earth.
passages.original: Εἶχε μὲν οὖν καὶ ἡ πρώτη δικαιώματα λατρείας τό τε ἅγιον κοσμικόν

passages.text: A tabernacle was prepared. In its first room were the lampstand, the table, and the consecrated bread. This was called the Holy Place.
passages.sermon:
God gave the people of Israel a covenant.
This covenant included a special place for worship.
They built a tabernacle.
The tabernacle had different rooms.
The first room was called the Holy Place.
In the Holy Place stood a lampstand.
There was also a table in the Holy Place.
On the table was the consecrated bread.
passages.original: σκηνὴ γὰρ κατεσκευάσθη ἡ πρώτη ἐν ᾗ ἥ τε λυχνία καὶ ἡ τράπεζα καὶ ἡ πρόθεσις τῶν ἄρτων ἥτις λέγεται Ἅγια

passages.text: Behind the second curtain was a room called the Most Holy Place, containing the golden altar of incense and the gold-covered ark of the covenant. Inside the ark were the gold jar of manna, Aaron’s staff that had budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant.
passages.sermon:
The first covenant had an earthly sanctuary.
Behind the second curtain was a special room.
People called this room the Most Holy Place.
The Most Holy Place contained the golden altar of incense.
It also contained the ark of the covenant.
The ark was covered with gold on all sides.
Inside the ark was a gold jar filled with manna.
Inside the ark was also Aaron’s staff that had budded.
Inside the ark were the stone tablets of the covenant.
passages.original: μετὰ δὲ τὸ δεύτερον καταπέτασμα σκηνὴ ἡ λεγομένη Ἅγια ἁγίων χρυσοῦν ἔχουσα θυμιατήριον καὶ τὴν κιβωτὸν τῆς διαθήκης περικεκαλυμμένην πάντοθεν χρυσίῳ ἐν ᾗ στάμνος χρυσῆ ἔχουσα τὸ μάννα καὶ ἡ ῥάβδος Ἀαρὼν ἡ βλαστήσασα καὶ αἱ πλάκες τῆς διαθήκης

passages.text: Above the ark were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy seat. But we cannot discuss these things in detail now.
passages.sermon: Above the ark were the cherubim of glory.\r\nThe cherubim overshadowed the mercy seat.\r\nWe cannot discuss these things in detail now.
passages.original: ὑπεράνω δὲ αὐτῆς Χερουβὶν δόξης κατασκιάζοντα τὸ ἱλαστήριον περὶ ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν νῦν λέγειν κατὰ μέρος

passages.text: When everything had been prepared in this way, the priests entered regularly into the first room to perform their sacred duties.
passages.sermon:
The priests served God in the tabernacle.
They entered the first room often.
They went in to perform their sacred duties.
They did this after everything was prepared as God commanded.
passages.original: Τούτων δὲ οὕτως κατεσκευασμένων εἰς μὲν τὴν πρώτην σκηνὴν διὰ παντὸς εἰσίασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς τὰς λατρείας ἐπιτελοῦντες

passages.text: But only the high priest entered the second room, and then only once a year, and never without blood, which he offered for himself and for the sins the people had committed in ignorance.
passages.sermon:
The high priest entered the second room.
He entered alone.
He entered only once each year.
He never entered without blood.
He offered the blood for himself.
He also offered the blood for the sins the people had committed in ignorance.
passages.original: εἰς δὲ τὴν δευτέραν ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ μόνος ὁ ἀρχιερεύς οὐ χωρὶς αἵματος ὃ προσφέρει ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ ἀγνοημάτων

passages.text: By this arrangement the Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Most Holy Place had not yet been disclosed as long as the first tabernacle was still standing.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit showed something important.
The Holy Spirit used this arrangement to teach.
The way into the Most Holy Place was not open yet.
The first tabernacle still stood at that time.
God had not revealed the way into His presence while the first tabernacle remained.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δηλοῦντος τοῦ Πνεύματος τοῦ Ἁγίου μήπω πεφανερῶσθαι τὴν τῶν ἁγίων ὁδὸν ἔτι τῆς πρώτης σκηνῆς ἐχούσης στάσιν

passages.text: It is an illustration for the present time, because the gifts and sacrifices being offered were unable to cleanse the conscience of the worshiper.
passages.sermon:
This is an illustration for the present time.
People offer gifts and sacrifices.
These gifts and sacrifices cannot make the worshiper perfect in conscience.
They cannot cleanse the worshiper's conscience.
passages.original: ἥτις παραβολὴ εἰς τὸν καιρὸν τὸν ἐνεστηκότα καθ’ ἣν δῶρά τε καὶ θυσίαι προσφέρονται μὴ δυνάμεναι κατὰ συνείδησιν τελειῶσαι τὸν λατρεύοντα

passages.text: They consist only in food and drink and special washings—external regulations imposed until the time of reform.
passages.sermon:
These rules are about food.
These rules are about drink.
These rules are about different kinds of washings.
These rules are only outward regulations.
These rules affect the body.
God gave these rules for a limited time.
God planned these rules to last until the time of reform.
passages.original: μόνον ἐπὶ βρώμασιν καὶ πόμασιν καὶ διαφόροις βαπτισμοῖς δικαιώματα σαρκὸς μέχρι καιροῦ διορθώσεως ἐπικείμενα

passages.text: But when Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come, He went through the greater and more perfect tabernacle that is not made by hands and is not a part of this creation.
passages.sermon:
Christ came.
Christ became high priest.
He brought the good things that have come.
He went through a tabernacle.
This tabernacle is greater and more perfect.
People did not make this tabernacle.
This tabernacle does not belong to this creation.
passages.original: Χριστὸς δὲ παραγενόμενος ἀρχιερεὺς τῶν γενομένων ἀγαθῶν διὰ τῆς μείζονος καὶ τελειοτέρας σκηνῆς οὐ χειροποιήτου τοῦτ’ ἔστιν οὐ ταύτης τῆς κτίσεως

passages.text: He did not enter by the blood of goats and calves, but He entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption.
passages.sermon:
Christ is the high priest.
Christ did not enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of goats and calves.
Christ entered the Most Holy Place by His own blood.
Christ entered once for all.
Christ secured eternal redemption.
passages.original: οὐδὲ δι’ αἵματος τράγων καὶ μόσχων διὰ δὲ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος εἰσῆλθεν ἐφάπαξ εἰς τὰ ἅγια αἰωνίαν λύτρωσιν εὑράμενος

passages.text: For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean sanctify them so that their bodies are clean, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, purify our consciences from works of death, so that we may serve the living God!
passages.sermon:
The blood of goats and bulls was used in sacrifices.
The ashes of a heifer were also used in rituals.
Priests sprinkled these on people who were ceremonially unclean.
This made their bodies clean.
These sacrifices only purified the flesh.
Christ is the Son of God.
Christ offered Himself to God.
He was perfect and without fault.
He did this through the eternal Spirit.
The blood of Christ is much greater than animal sacrifices.
The blood of Christ can purify our consciences.
It cleanses us from dead works.
This allows us to serve the living God.
passages.original: Εἰ γὰρ τὸ αἷμα τράγων καὶ ταύρων καὶ σποδὸς δαμάλεως ῥαντίζουσα τοὺς κεκοινωμένους ἁγιάζει πρὸς τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς καθαρότητα πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὸ αἷμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὃς διὰ Πνεύματος αἰωνίου ἑαυτὸν προσήνεγκεν ἄμωμον τῷ Θεῷ καθαριεῖ τὴν συνείδησιν ἡμῶν ἀπὸ νεκρῶν ἔργων εἰς τὸ λατρεύειν Θεῷ ζῶντι

passages.text: Therefore Christ is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance, now that He has died to redeem them from the transgressions committed under the first covenant.
passages.sermon:
Christ is the mediator of a new covenant.
He became mediator because He died.
His death redeems people from the transgressions committed under the first covenant.
God calls certain people.
These called people receive the promised eternal inheritance.
They receive this inheritance because Christ died for their redemption.
passages.original: Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο διαθήκης καινῆς μεσίτης ἐστίν ὅπως θανάτου γενομένου εἰς ἀπολύτρωσιν τῶν ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ διαθήκῃ παραβάσεων τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν λάβωσιν οἱ κεκλημένοι τῆς αἰωνίου κληρονομίας

passages.text: In the case of a will, it is necessary to establish the death of the one who made it, because a will does not take effect until the one who made it has died; it cannot be executed while he is still alive.
passages.sermon:
A will is a legal document.
A will gives instructions for what happens after a person dies.
A will only takes effect after the person who made it dies.
A will does not have power while the person is still alive.
The death of the one who made the will must be established.
Only then can the will be put into effect.
passages.original: Ὅπου γὰρ διαθήκη θάνατον ἀνάγκη φέρεσθαι τοῦ διαθεμένου διαθήκη γὰρ ἐπὶ νεκροῖς βεβαία ἐπεὶ μή‿ ποτε ἰσχύει ὅτε ζῇ ὁ διαθέμενος

passages.text: That is why even the first covenant was not put into effect without blood.
passages.sermon: The first covenant was the agreement God made with His people through Moses.\r\nGod did not put the first covenant into effect without blood.\r\nBlood was necessary to establish the first covenant.
passages.original: Ὅθεν οὐδὲ ἡ πρώτη χωρὶς αἵματος ἐνκεκαίνισται

passages.text: For when Moses had proclaimed every commandment of the law to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, along with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled the scroll and all the people, saying, “This is the blood of the covenant, which God has commanded you to keep.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
God gave Moses commandments for the people.
Moses spoke every commandment of the law to all the people.
Moses took the blood of calves and goats.
He also took water, scarlet wool, and hyssop.
Moses sprinkled the scroll with the blood.
He also sprinkled all the people with the blood.
Moses said, “This is the blood of the covenant.”
God commanded you to keep this covenant.
passages.original: λαληθείσης γὰρ πάσης ἐντολῆς κατὰ τὸν νόμον ὑπὸ Μωϋσέως παντὶ τῷ λαῷ λαβὼν τὸ αἷμα τῶν μόσχων καὶ τῶν τράγων μετὰ ὕδατος καὶ ἐρίου κοκκίνου καὶ ὑσσώπου αὐτό τε τὸ βιβλίον καὶ πάντα τὸν λαὸν ἐράντισεν λέγων Τοῦτο τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης ἧς ἐνετείλατο πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὁ Θεός

passages.text: In the same way, he sprinkled with blood the tabernacle and all the vessels used in worship.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses sprinkled blood on the tabernacle.
He also sprinkled blood on all the vessels used in worship.
He did this in the same way as before.
passages.original: Καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν δὲ καὶ πάντα τὰ σκεύη τῆς λειτουργίας τῷ αἵματι ὁμοίως ἐράντισεν

passages.text: According to the law, in fact, nearly everything must be purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
passages.sermon:
The law of Moses required purification.
Almost everything had to be purified with blood.
Blood was necessary for cleansing.
Without the shedding of blood, there is no forgiveness.
Forgiveness does not happen without blood being shed.
passages.original: καὶ σχεδὸν ἐν αἵματι πάντα καθαρίζεται κατὰ τὸν νόμον καὶ χωρὶς αἱματεκχυσίας οὐ γίνεται ἄφεσις

passages.text: So it was necessary for the copies of the heavenly things to be purified with these sacrifices, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
passages.sermon:
The law required sacrifices for purification.
Priests purified the tabernacle and its vessels with blood.
These things were copies of heavenly things.
God commanded that these earthly copies be purified with animal sacrifices.
The true heavenly things needed better sacrifices.
God required greater sacrifices for the real things in heaven.
passages.original: Ἀνάγκη οὖν τὰ μὲν ὑποδείγματα τῶν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς τούτοις καθαρίζεσθαι αὐτὰ δὲ τὰ ἐπουράνια κρείττοσιν θυσίαις παρὰ ταύτας

passages.text: For Christ did not enter a man-made copy of the true sanctuary, but He entered heaven itself, now to appear on our behalf in the presence of God.
passages.sermon:
Christ is the Son of God.
Christ did not enter a sanctuary made by human hands.
That sanctuary was only a copy of the true one.
Christ entered heaven itself.
He now appears in the presence of God.
He appears there for us.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ εἰς χειροποίητα εἰσῆλθεν ἅγια Χριστός ἀντίτυπα τῶν ἀληθινῶν ἀλλ’ εἰς αὐτὸν τὸν οὐρανόν νῦν ἐμφανισθῆναι τῷ προσώπῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν

passages.text: Nor did He enter heaven to offer Himself again and again, as the high priest enters the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own.
passages.sermon:
Christ did not enter heaven to offer Himself many times.
The high priest enters the Most Holy Place every year.
The high priest brings blood that is not his own.
Christ did not do this.
Christ did not offer Himself again and again.
passages.original: οὐδ’ ἵνα πολλάκις προσφέρῃ ἑαυτόν ὥσπερ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἰσέρχεται εἰς τὰ ἅγια κατ’ ἐνιαυτὸν ἐν αἵματι ἀλλοτρίῳ

passages.text: Otherwise, Christ would have had to suffer repeatedly since the foundation of the world. But now He has appeared once for all at the end of the ages to do away with sin by the sacrifice of Himself.
passages.sermon:
Christ is the Son of God.
Christ did not suffer many times since the world began.
If repeated suffering were needed, Christ would have suffered again and again from the foundation of the world.
But Christ appeared once for all at the end of the ages.
Christ came to remove sin.
He did this by offering Himself as a sacrifice.
passages.original: Ἐπεὶ ἔδει αὐτὸν πολλάκις παθεῖν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου νυνὶ δὲ ἅπαξ ἐπὶ συντελείᾳ τῶν αἰώνων εἰς ἀθέτησιν τῆς ἁμαρτίας διὰ τῆς θυσίας αὐτοῦ πεφανέρωται

passages.text: Just as man is appointed to die once, and after that to face judgment, so also Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many; and He will appear a second time, not to bear sin, but to bring salvation to those who eagerly await Him.
passages.sermon:
Every person must die once.
After death, every person faces judgment.
Christ is the Son of God.
God appointed Christ to be offered once.
Christ was offered to bear the sins of many people.
Christ will appear a second time.
When Christ appears again, He will not bear sin.
Christ will bring salvation.
He will bring salvation to those who eagerly wait for Him.
passages.original: Καὶ καθ’ ὅσον ἀπόκειται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ἅπαξ ἀποθανεῖν μετὰ δὲ τοῦτο κρίσις οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστός ἅπαξ προσενεχθεὶς εἰς τὸ πολλῶν ἀνενεγκεῖν ἁμαρτίας ἐκ δευτέρου χωρὶς ἁμαρτίας ὀφθήσεται τοῖς αὐτὸν ἀπεκδεχομένοις εἰς σωτηρίαν
